# What is R?
R is a popular statistical programming language used across disciplines (e.g. environmental sciences, geography, epidemiology, medical statistics). Other popular statistical programming languages include MATLAB, Python, Stata and SPSS. R can be used to conduct analyses and produce tables and graphs. You can find more information about R on the [official website](https://www.r-project.org/about.html).

# What is RStudio?
RStudio is an integrated development environment (IDE) specifically designed for R. RStudio is an application which brings all the tools you need into one place in order to write code and run analyses. It is somewhat comparable with the user interface for SPSS or Stata. It is possible to run R from the command line, but unless you are an advanced user, we suggest running DataSHIELD within RStudio.

# Installing R & RStudio
To install R, you can follow the instructions [here](https://cloud.r-project.org/). 
To install RStudio, follow the instructions [here](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/).

# Installing the core DataSHIELD packages
Once you have installed R and RStudio you can install the specific packages needed to run DataSHIELD. Here is an [overview](https://wiki.datashield.org/en/opmanag/core-packages) of the core DataSHIELD packages and what they do. To install these packages use the following script:
```{r}
install.packages(c("DSI", "DSOpal", "DSMolgenisArmadillo"))
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("datashield/dsBaseClient")
```

# Install additional R development packages
To develop in R, you need three further packages:
- [`usethis`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=usethis) automates common tasks in setting up an R package.
- [`devtools`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=devtools) contains tools for developing, testing and releasing r packages.
- [`DSLite`](https://cran.r-project.org/package=DSLite) mimics the behaviour of a remote DataSHIELD server, and speeds up the development cycle.

```r
install.packages(c("usethis", "devtools", "DSLite"))
```

And those can be loaded in your working environment with the following commands:
```r
library(usethis)
library(devtools)
library(DSLite)
```
